ca_4_little_wing_area.blurb: A small cliff set in talus on Yosemite Valley's north side, just west of Ribbon Falls. It has nine traditional routes, all on a single pitch. Five are 5.7 to 5.8, with the rest running from 5.10a up to 5.10d, so it suits a leader who wants moderate to mid-5.10 crack and face climbing without a long day. The granite is solid, and a couple of other small cliffs sit within a short walk if you want more mileage. Expect a hike across talus and slide debris to reach the base.

ca_south_rock_2.blurb: One of three sandstone formations at Footsteps Rock on the far north coast, with a few steep faces that lean out over the Pacific. It has nine bolted routes, one of them a two-pitch line, spanning 5.9 up to 5.13. Most of the grades land in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, so this is a place for climbers already comfortable pulling hard. Holds are bubbly and pocketed, giving the wall an unusual texture. The rock quality around the three formations varies from crisp and compact to grainy.

_expect.name: Cirque of the Climbables - Right Side

ca_cirque_of_the_climbables_right_side.blurb: A cluster of nine traditional routes on Queen Mountain in Joshua Tree National Park, forming the right half of the Cirque of the Climbables. The grades are broad, from a couple of 5.4 lines and some 5.6 to 5.8 climbs to three at 5.10. That makes it a good fit for a mixed party with leaders at different levels. The walk in follows an old road north from the parking circle and then a cairned trail that gains height steadily, taking somewhere between thirty and fifty minutes.

_expect.name: Swedish House Mafia Boulders / Hill Top Area.

ca_swedish_house_mafia_boulders_hill_top.blurb: A geometric stack of boulders at the far east end of the Hill Top cluster in North San Diego County, looking over the sport park. It holds nine problems, and most are low-grade: a few at the easiest end, several around V1, a V3 to V4, and one much harder V6 arete. That mix works for beginners and for people warming up before moving elsewhere in the cirque. The approach follows the field and then a concrete drainage ditch uphill from the parking lot. Lights from the nearby sports fields can illuminate the boulders after dark.

ca_real_cloud_ripper_tower_the.blurb: The largest rock mass in the Cloud Ripper Towers cirque, near Tahquitz and Suicide Rocks at about 7,800 feet. Nine traditionally protected routes climb its face, running from 5.6 to 5.10, and most sit at 5.8 or below. The tower is covered in knobs, buckets and splitter cracks. Several lines carry a run-out or PG13 rating, so confident placements and a steady head matter here more than the grade alone suggests.

ca_potter_s_point.blurb: A small crag in a pine forest high above Santa Barbara, with views over the ocean, the Channel Islands, Goleta and the city. It has nine routes: seven bolted lines and two top ropes, mostly short. Grades run from 5.8 through to a 5.13a, with a good cluster around 5.10 and a few 5.11 and 5.12 lines for stronger climbers. Light traffic means some lichen on the holds. Expect a bit of trail-less scrambling between routes after the main path ends.
ca_potter_s_point.parking_note: Drive up Gibraltar Road from town to where it meets East Camino Cielo, and use the turnout on the left just short of the junction.
